My season is almost over, so I want to highlight the better shows. This season wasn't particularly good. The best anime were sequels to already-good shows, and the few, good non-sequels weren't great. I'll tell you what might be worth watching, and why you may like it. I'll give my score at the end of each pitch. Scroll down, here, for an outline of my scoring system.

After much truncating and slashing of words, I have decided to allocate the non-sequels to a comment because I'm tired of fighting with Voat over how many characters this post is.

SEQUELS

If you've watched the original, you're probably planning on watching the sequel, so I'll pitch the original anime, and compare it to the sequel.

1. JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Stardust Crusaders 2nd Season:

A sequel to JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Stardust Crusaders, which is a sequel to JoJo's Bizarre Adventure (2012), which I pitched here. In short, JoJo is an amazing series about big dudes fighting other big dudes using crazy superpowers. There's so much manliness that you have to watch Non Non Biyori afterwards to center yourself. This show is great. It'll make you laugh at the exaggerated situations and reactions. It'll make you cry at the manly sacrifices. And you'll get really pumped whenever there's a fight. I cannot praise this series enough.

Stadust Crusaders is a tad different than the original JoJo. SC follows a more "Villain of the Week" format than the origina, but not to its detriment. I didn't enjoy it as much as the more condensed plot of the first series, but each of the characers in SC have their own charm, their own crazy powers, and their own overdone responses to events. SC retains the humor and intensity of the original JoJo; I recommend it to anyone who enjoyed the first series.

Score: 8

2. Yahari Ore no Seishun Love Comedy wa Machigatteiru. Zoku

A sequel to Yahari Ore no Seishun Love Comedy wa Machigatteiru. (a.k.a. Oregariu), which, despite its title, is not a romcom. I watched the first season a year ago, and don't feel comfortable pitching it. I plan to re-watch the first and second seasons, and may write a recommendation, then. The reason that I believe that the 2nd season is worth watching is because it is the most realistic portrayal of high school that I've seen in anime. There's no overdramatic love confessions or high-stakes competitions against rivals. Instead, Oregairu is a subdued examination of the relationship between the main character, Hikigaya Hachiman, and his fellow club members, Yui Yuigahama and Yukino Yukinoshita.

Hikigaya is a member of the Service Club, in which he, Yui, and Yukino must accept student requests for help. The show examines each of the characters' motivations and methods for dealing with the requests. The show centers on Hikigaya, who, despite his cynical facade, is actually an intricate person who is seeking something. The show follows this group as they contend with small problems, as well as huge issues that may tear them apart. Can Hikigaya preserve his tenuous relationship with Yui and Yukino while searching for that which he desires? As we explore this question, we see that people aren't always who they appear to be, and they don't always want what they say they want. Oregairu 2 shines because it examines such nuanced questions deftly.

Score: 7

3. Fate/stay night: Unlimited Blade Works (TV) 2nd Season

The chronology of this one is a little complicated. F/sn: UBW (TV) 2nd Season is the 2nd half of an adaptation of the second route (UBW) of the F/sn visual novel. The 1st route is called Fate, which does not have a worthy anime adaptation. The 3rd route is called Heaven's Feel, and will receieve a movie some time in the future. Basically, the F/sn VN is split into 3 routes, which are extreme variations of the same story. These 3 routes are separate stories that are not tied together, but each route builds upon information discovered by the reader in the previous routes. In case you're wondering Fate/Zero is an adaptation of a prequel light novel written by a separate author.

As someone who was a fan of F/Z, proceeded to play the VN, and then watched the UBW anime, let me offer this advice: If you like F/Z because of its themes and writing style, then you may not like F/sn. The source materials are written by different authors who have different outlooks and styles. However, if you like the setting and the premise, then you may like F/sn. If you really like the world of the Fate franchise, then my advice is to play the VN.

If you like the world of the Fate franchise, but can't be conviced to play a VN, or if you kind of like the Fate franchise and want to see some more or if you have no idea what this is, but it seems interesting, then watch the prologue and first season of this anime. If you don't like it, then don't hold that against F/Z. They are separate works that can be enjoyed in isolation.

The premise of this show is that 7 mages have been chosen by the Holy Grail to participate in a war to obtain the power to grant any wish. In order to fight this war, 7 Servants (Heroic Spirits from all time) are summoned to serve 7 Masters. What this show boils down to is a lot of exposition, punctuated by beautifully animated fight scenes. If you're not sure how that sounds, then watch the prologue and give the show a few episodes. If the fight scenes and philosophy aren't doing it for you, then it's not gonna get better.

Personally, I'm not a fan of the themes or exposition of UBW as much as I was of F/Z. The fight scenes, however, are undeniably amazing, and they can make the show. There are also some very intense story moments that will have your jaw on the floor. However, this show is not for everyone.

Score: 7

I take it this is a thread to talk about how we felt about shows from last season then? Alright, I'll write up my thoughts of the show I completed from last season

Assassination Classroom - As the season was beginning, I will be fair and say this show was starting to lose interest on me. The little-by-little development of individual characters before moving on was leaving me uninterested, and the constant assassination attempts wasn't interesting me, because I knew that they wouldn't kill Koro-Sensei before the end of the show. But the whole island arc at the end of the season really saved the show for me. It stopped being about individuals and starting treating everyone as a whole, which is what I felt was stronger for the show. Spoilers for the arc I hope that for the next season, we will get more stories like the Island arc and not the earlier episodes. Better individual character development as well, as I didn't feel that connected to the individual characters, but more so the collective

Fate/Stay Night: Unlimited Blade Works 2nd Season - sigh See, I just came off of watching Fate/Zero from finishing UBW, and I ended up having a much more enjoyable time watching that than this. I won't go around and say UBW S2 was completely horrible - the character development with Archer was pretty good, and the fights are really great to watch, but I didn't particularly care for it. With Fate/Zero, they spent time focusing on each different character allowing you to properly get an idea on who they are before the fights happened, which was quite effective when characters ended up being killed. UBW was too busy focused on Shirou (who I just do not like whatsoever) and Rin (who was just underdeveloped), so spoilers I think the perspective of the story within UBW in comparison to Zero is worse. And that left me quite disinterested within the show. It's a shame, because I know this story can be done right. If I did rewatch this show, I feel like I might enjoy myself more, now that I've seen Zero and I've seen some more development on characters, but it wasn't an completely enjoyable watch

Kekkai Sensen - This hasn't finished yet of course, so I can't have a complete opinion on the show, but this has got to be my AOTS. It feels like something which could have come from Hiroyuki Imaishi (Gurren Lagann, Kill la Kill). Whilst the show doesn't exactly excel within storytelling, the show itself is really enjoyable to watch, and the stylisation is awesome. The show knows when to take itself seriously and to not, and it works well for the fight scenes. The setting for the show (with the soundtrack in tail) is rather unique in comparison to other anime, and it helps to diversify the show. It makes great usage of it within the storytelling. The fight scenes were filled with ridiculous action, and that really works well for me. The background story with Leonardo and White should have gotten some more airtime, and other characters should have spent some time getting some development (it was annoying to see characters introduced in one episode, then failing to show up again for a number of episodes). But when I watched this show, I wasn't expecting to see that. I wasn't expecting a show with a deep, solid story to it. I was expecting something which was enjoyable to watch, and I got that again and again and that's why I loved watching it.

Nisekoi: - I don't know what I'm doing anymore. This show does not have a good setting to it and I don't have a good attachment to the characters, which is what I search for within slice of life shows. I still have no idea why I can't stop watching Nisekoi. I can only really chalk it up to the Shaft animation style. I...I just don't know what to say about Nisekoi: really.

Ore Monogatari - I can't help but feel like this show could have only done with a single cour. Whilst the show has gone past the forbidden line with romance/slice of life anime and actually have a couple present within the show, it hasn't particularly done a lot with this concept. It was enjoyable at first, but as the show kept on going and sort-of forcing the whole "Man, Takeo and Yamato are such a great couple, aren't they?" angle, I'm growing less interested within the show. Another thing I'm not liking about the show is the whole "Takeo is a literal superhuman angle". It was odd and humourous at the beginning, but once they kept on beating the horse to death, it became tiring to watch. However, if the show toned down those angles and increased other elements within the show, like issues within the couple (for example, the differences in the strength of the relationship between Takeo and Yamato), I feel like it could have been better. Those issues could be perfectly well explored within 12 episodes in contrast to 24. Sunakawa is a good character as well, and spoilers was one of the highlights for me within the show as well. When the show is good, it can be a great slice-of-life, but the lesser moments of the show does end up bringing this down for me

OreGairu Zoku - There's something I like about Oregairu's different take on shows with high-school settings. The majority of characters in the show end up being flawed, and the show is unafriad to show that, instead of just tucking it away like other shows. That helped make the show good for me. The character development ends up being more effective, making all of the events which transpire between characters way more effective. Spoilers There also felt like there was more breathing room with this season in comparison to the first one, which was great as I felt the first season did go quite fast at times. Could have used an extra episode or two at the end though. And more Saika.

Huh, I never even thought of that. In order for this theory to be true, Voat would have to be assuming that the increase in value to Bitcoin will outpace the added money they would raised by setting up a Kickstarter. Here's my two-premise argument for why that might not be the correct assumption:

1. The increase in the value of Bitcoins that would result from a few new investors in the currency is not likely to outpace the amount that would be lost by not setting up a Kickstarter. Example: Let's say that for every 3 people who want to donate to Voat, 1 already has Bitcoin to donate, 1 is willing to buy into Bitcoin in order to donate but would also donate to a Kickstarter, and 1 will only donate via Kickstarter. By not setting up a kickstarter, they are losing out on that third donation. Therefore, in order for their decision to force people to use Bitcoin to be worth it, the increase in the value of Voat's Bitcoins that results from the second person buying in would have to be greater than the amount that the third person would have donated directly to Voat.

2. With kickstarter, Voat gets to internalize 100% of the added benefit it gets from deciding to open up Kickstarter as a viable option, whereas any increase in Bitcoin's value that results from Voat's actions would be dispersed amongst ALL Bitcoin holders. Even if Kickstarter only gives you, say, $0.80 for every dollar donated, that means Voat still takes home 80% of the benefit they have generated. But with any increase in the value of Bitcoin that Voat stimulates, they share that value increase with every single other person in the world who owns bitcoin. In order to capitalize upon their value-add in the same proportion, Voat would have to own 80% of all the Bitcoin that exist in the world. Now of course, it is possible that the increase in Bitcoin value could still break even, or even exceed the value add from using Kickstarter as a parallel in terms of real dollars, but I see that as unlikely.

All that being said, I know very little about Bitcoin and I'm also not an economist. I'm just trying to contribute to the discussion and help make Voat a robust marketplace of ideas!

David Anderson wrote:

BOINC's funding from the U.S. National Science Foundation has ended, at least for the time being. This funding supported me, Rom Walton, and Charlie Fenton. We're now working on other things, although we'll stay involved in BOINC at some level.

The BOINC project will continue, and will be run according to a community-based model rather than centrally. In essence, the people who contribute to BOINC now make the decisions about it. This model is summarized here: http://boinc.berkeley.edu/trac/wiki/ProjectGovernance and described in detail here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C6pU5RqidYBxk9oyAevm1yH1tn4Hw27oM8YpvsnR-gg

There will probably be little visible change. The BOINC software will continue to work. The translation system, Alpha testing project, BOINC web site,message boards, and email lists will continue to operate. However, any new development and major bug fixes to BOINC will need to be done by volunteer programmers. I'm confident that the BOINC community will meet the challenge.

I welcome your feedback. Please post it to boinc_admin@googlegroups.com, a new email list for discussions about the BOINC project as a whole.

-- David
The BOINC project has transitioned to a community-based governance model.
